short: Cross-attention EEG-EMG fusion is new among EEG-EMG decoders but rests on a five-fold ablation with no seed count; no EEG-only result, and the subject adversary adds 0.41 points.
position: The paper changes EEG-EMG fusion (M06), EEG channel selection (M05) and adversarial subject removal (M03); all three are standard. Bidirectional cross-attention is absent from the 30 ledger studies recording both EEG and EMG, but the ablation behind it is a five-fold average with no stated seed count in which every ablated network falls about 10 points, below a DeepConvNet fed concatenated EEG and EMG (86.56% against 88.08%). The 20-channel subset loses 0.37 points against the full EEG set while EMG stays in every configuration, and no EEG-only or EMG-only model is reported. The subject discriminator adds 0.41 points of leave-one-subject-out accuracy, with no seed count stated. The leave-one-subject-out mean of 85.10% over ten subjects (53.33% to 95.00%) uses no test-subject data despite its Calibration heading, but the five-fold split unit, channel-selection data, early-stopping data and seeds are not stated.
